newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC approves Duke Power, PanEnergy merger.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC approves Duke Power, PanEnergy merger.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday approved the $7.7 billion merger of Duke Power Co. and PanEnergy Corp..
The commissioners said this application was easy to approve because the two companies had completely separate service territories.
"Approval of this merger was not especially difficult," Commissioner William Massey said.

The commissioners said the union of the big utility with the natural gas marketing and pipeline company would not result in increased market concentration of generation or electric transmission assets in any geographical market.
"The merger is unlikely to have any appreciable effect on competition," Commissioner Donald Santa said at the commission meeting.

The commission also found that PanEnergy would not be able to restrict natural gas supplies in order to increase gas prices to Duke's competitors, because other companies in Duke's area had access to enough competing gas supplies.
This was the second so-called convergence merger approved by the FERC under its new merger policy. The application was approved within four months of being filed.
A spokesman for Duke Power said Tuesday that assuming the commission approved the union to form Duke Energy, the companies expected to close their deal this summer.

Duke Power has 1.8 million customers in North Carolina and South Carolina. PanEnergy is considered the second largest natural gas pipeline company and third largest natural gas marketer in the United States.
